candidates.description: A scale used to assess how a patient's disease affects their daily living abilities.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the numeric value associated with 'ECOG' or 'ECOG performance status'.
candidates.measurement_definition: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale, where 0 indicates fully active and 4 indicates completely disabled.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the status was assessed at the time of diagnosis or at the specific time of the oncology visit is not always explicitly stated.

citations.quote: No radiographic evidence of intracranial metastatic disease.
brain metastases present (treated right frontal lesion, untreated left cerebellar lesion)
two enhancing lesions in the left cerebellum and right frontal lobe
Brain MRI negative for intracranial metastases.

candidates.description: The presence or absence of metastatic cancer cells in the brain as determined by radiographic imaging.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Review 'Brain MRI' or 'Impression' sections for the presence of intracranial lesions or a statement of no metastatic disease.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if brain MRI or PET/CT identifies enhancing lesions, metastatic foci, or 'brain metastases present'; negative if imaging reports 'no radiographic evidence of intracranial metastatic disease' or 'Brain MRI negative for intracranial metastases'.
candidates.name: Presence of Brain Metastases
candidates.uncertainty: The timing of the MRI relative to other baseline assessments may vary between patients.

limitations: The evidence consists of fragmented clinical notes, which may omit complementary baseline data.
The number of patients represented in the evidence is small, limiting the diversity of the observed variable ranges.
summary: The provided evidence supports the identification of baseline patient characteristics in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cases, specifically regarding functional status (ECOG performance status) and the presence of intracranial metastatic disease.
